function.mechanism: Acts as a phosphate buffer and ionic-strength modifier; phosphate anions complex cations and support pH control, stabilization, and processing functions in food systems.

adi.basis: Group ADI expressed as phosphorus for phosphoric acid and phosphates (E338-341, E343, E450-452), EFSA re-evaluation 2019

efsa.key_finding: EFSA reduced the phosphate group ADI and reported that high consumers, especially children, may exceed the ADI under some scenarios.

adi.basis: Group MTDI as phosphorus for phosphoric acid and phosphates in WHO/JECFA summary

concerns.summary: High intake of readily absorbable inorganic phosphate additives is associated with increased phosphorus burden and concern for kidney-related outcomes; EFSA used nephrocalcinosis-related evidence in group ADI setting.
key_references: Dietary phosphorus burden and human health (2024 review)
Dietary Phosphates and Human Health (2025 review)

concerns.summary: Human and review evidence indicates phosphate additive intake can acutely raise phosphate-regulatory biomarkers (e.g., FGF23/PTH), with broader concern for cardiovascular risk at sustained high phosphorus burden.
key_references: Randomized crossover breakfast study in healthy adults (2017)
Dietary phosphorus burden and human health (2024 review)
Dietary Phosphates and Human Health (2025 review)

no_concern_confirmed: No specific IARC carcinogenic classification identified for magnesium phosphates in the current IARC classified-agents dataset.

populations: high consumers of phosphate-containing processed foods
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2019 exposure assessment indicated potential exceedance of the group ADI in young/high-intake groups under some scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: E343 remains authorized (EU/FDA) but with important caveats: EFSA set a stricter group ADI and identified possible exceedance in younger/high-intake populations, and human/mechanistic evidence supports concern at higher phosphate additive exposure.
key_factors: EFSA group ADI 40 mg/kg bw/day (as phosphorus) with exceedance concern
FDA GRAS status under GMP conditions
